<CENTRE> <SIZE:medium> Trough <LINE> <LI: <CENTRE> <SIZE:medium> 給餌桶 <LINE> <LINE> <LEFT> <SIZE:small> 給餌桶に食べ物を追加するには、容器内に餌を追加してください。 <LINE> 水を追加するには、給餌桶を右クリックして「水を加える」を選択します。 <LINE> 給餌桶には食べ物か水のどちらか一方のみ入れられます。 <LINE> <LINE> 給餌桶は動物が利用できるよう、家畜ゾーン内に設置してください。
<CENTRE> <SIZE:medium> Animal Trailer <L: <CENTRE> <SIZE:medium> 動物トレーラー <LINE> <LINE> <LEFT> <SIZE:small> 動物をトレーラーに入れるには、後部ドア付近まで誘導し、トレーラーを右クリックします。 <LINE> 小動物も同様に入れることができます。 <LINE> <LINE> 動物はトレーラー内の食料容器から餌を食べられます。 <LINE> 直接餌を与えるか、右クリックで水を与えることもできます。 <LINE> ニワトリはトレーラー内の巣箱に卵を産みます。 <LINE> 各トレーラーには容量があり、動物の種類や大きさに応じて使用されます。 <LINE> トレーラーが移動中は、内部の動物に徐々にストレスがかかります。
<CENTRE> <SIZE:medium> Livestock Zones <: <CENTRE> <SIZE:medium> 家畜ゾーン <LINE> <LINE> <LEFT> <SIZE:small> 動物がさまよわないようにするには、家畜ゾーン内にいる必要があります。 <LINE> 画面左上の「家畜ゾーン」アイコンをクリックし、「ゾーンを追加」を選択します。 クリックとドラッグで新しいゾーンを作成します。 <LINE> 隣接するゾーンは1つの大きなゾーンとして扱われます。 <LINE> <LINE> 動物は指定ゾーン内に留まる傾向がありますが、ストレスを感じると逃げ出します。 <LINE> 防ぐには、ゾーンの周囲に囲いを作ってください。 <LINE> <LINE> ゾーン内のマスを右クリックし、「~を確認」を選択すると、 動物、飼育小屋、食料などの情報を確認できます。 <LINE> <LINE> 動物はゾーン内の屋根付きのエリアを認識し、雨天時にはその下で雨宿りします。

Despite an overwhelming early response following the tornado on April 18, which saw ample aid provided for residents in the aftermath, promised federal funds for re- building have still not arrived, with buildings patched up with wood, and major damage still evident.                                                      Early warnings meant many residents were taking shelter when the tornado touched down in the northeast part of town, but the high winds killed three residents and injured dozens. The virus is in Louisville. Several of us here are running fevers, and there are hundreds of infected in the streets.         We wish to thank all our readers for being with us through these unprecedented times. If you are one of the few immune, you are the steward of a new world. It's now your duty to carry on the light of humanity and civilization. Even a single candle will cut through the deepest darkness.                                   May God have mercy on the rest of us and our loved ones.<type:text, x:780, y:265, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0.5, pivotY:0, scaleX:1, scaleY:1, textLeading:-4, font:SdfOldBold>Despair grips^nation, world<type:text, x:770, y:350, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, pivotX:0.5, pivotY:0, scaleX:0.6, scaleY:0.6, textLeading:-4, font:SdfOldBold>    Handful Immune^     to 'Aerial Strain'<type:text, x:672, y:415, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.45, scaleY:0.45, autoWidth:493.33, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>       The CDC has confirmed that the Knox Virus spreads rapidly through the air, although a small percentage of people are immune to the "aerial variant" of the virus. For everyone else, the likelihood of a cure or treatment is now close to zero. Help your elderly and vulnerable neighbors. Share food if you have more than you need. Avoid crowds at all costs.                                 As we saw at the boundary, gunfire attracts them. Have a baseball bat or other easy-to-use weapon ready and don't be afraid to attack them. Once they die and come back, they only want to spread the virus.<type:text, x:590, y:600, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.26, scaleY:0.26, font:SdfRegular>AFFILIATED PRESS<type:text, x:247, y:615, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.45, scaleY:0.45, autoWidth:911.11, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldBold>A group of infected photographed by one of our team on the way to our offices on Thursday, near downtown Louisville. Hundreds of military personnel, fully armed and in battle gear, arrived in the area early Tuesday morning, encircling thou- sands of civilians within the cordon, as well as displacing hundreds of people who live outside the boundary. Rumors abound of a military exercise, but all calls to army officials went unanswered.                      Telephone lines have also been down in the area for the last several days, making communication with the cordoned-off area almost impossible. And yet, despite attempts by many residents to look on the bright side and downplay the threat, it's clear many feel a gnawing anxiety about the Knox Virus.              Authorities are now saying that the virus, though deadly, spreads only through fluid contact, drawing comparisons to ebola outbreaks, which were eventually contained. But  there's  never  been an ebola outbreak so near to a major city, and some residents have already relocated over the Ohio River. Though the WHO lacks any legal authority to  enforce  the  advice, all flights were grounded almost immediately by airlines shocked at the sudden nature of the an- nouncement.                             In a White House briefing,  the  President has called the WHO's an- nouncement "unwelcome and economically un- sound".                                    Air Erin CEO Ryan Byrne  said,  "We  knew this was coming, but we thought  we'd  at  least have time to prepare. We have to  comply.  None  of us want to be responsible for an outbreak, but we have businesses to run. The  cure  can't  be worse than the disease.<type:text, x:180, y:716, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular> The earthquake, estimated at 7.5 on the Richter scale, created a tsunami which inundated parts of the island of Hokkaido and struck coast of southeastern Russia.             Hundreds of people are feared dead, with fires and a landslide reported in the town of Okushiri on the small island of the same name near Hokkaido. The city was previously struck by a strong earthquake last January, which killed two people and injured more than a thousand. Monday's quake was far more devastating,     with     the<type:texture, width:146, height:1, x:680, y:786, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9><type:text, x:826, y:798, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, pivotX:1, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>(See "Japan", A13)<type:text, x:15, y:195, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldBold>By Richard Carlson<type:text, x:15, y:211, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>Staff Writer<type:text, x:15, y:240, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:380, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>     KNOX EXCLUSION ZONE  BORDER,  Ky.  - A new photograph that emerged Monday of an in- fected, dismembered, but apparently still-living man in a street full of bodies in the town of West Point within the Knox Exclusion Zone has raised more questions about the government's response to the Knox Event.                        Thousands of resi- dents have been trapped within a cordoned-off zone of hundreds of square miles of Kentucky since July 6, with little commu- nication with the outside world.                                       The leaked picture has added yet more anger to the riots gripping cities nationwide, with curfews having little effect. The World Health Organ- ization has decried the hundreds of bomb and death threats against its headquarters and staff in Geneva,   calling   them "an extremely unhelpful response in a time of un- precedented crisis." Swiss police are closely monitor- ing the situation, which comes in the wake of the WHO's advice on July 11 for international flights worldwide to be grounded due to the Knox outbreak.        The advice, though voluntary, has been fol- lowed by almost every airline in the world, leav- ing millions of national and international travel- ers stranded, and forcing governments around the world to deal with the sudden stranding of vast numbers of tourists within their borders at the height<type:texture, width:146, height:1, x:680, y:786, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9><type:text, x:826, y:798, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, pivotX:1, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>(See "Threats", A11)<type:text, x:15, y:195, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldBold>By Keith Haroldson<type:text, x:15, y:211, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>Staff Writer<type:text, x:15, y:240, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>           NEW YORK, NY - Thirty-eight nations is- sued a joint statement through the United Na- tions denouncing what they termed a "complete lack of clarity" over the details of the Knox illness outbreak. The statement came hours after Gen. John McGrew, the mil- itary overseer of the Knox Containment Zone, said there was "no need for further panic" after the leaking of a gruesome photo from the Zone on Monday, along with con- firmation of extreme violence between the in- fected.                                    The President has left Washington, D.C., and could not be reached for comment.                                China was among the most vociferous critics of the US, with its dele- gates claiming the U.S. places, "the continued wealth of Wall Street above the common good of humanity", claims swiftly  condemned by U.S. allies.  Meanwhile, Vatican City<type:text, x:180, y:716, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>is being closed due to the threat of the Knox illness. The claims have called in question statements from the au- thorities that the sickness can spread only through bites and scratches.                 A CDC official said the emergence of aerial transmission represented, "a greater threat to hu- manity than the Spanish Flu or the Black Death". The WHO has said the virus is likely already around the world, and that its advice to ground flights "almost certainly came too late to make a difference." Screening programs for  the  illness<type:texture, width:146, height:1, x:680, y:786, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9><type:text, x:826, y:798, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, pivotX:1, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>(See "Virus", A11)<type:text, x:15, y:195, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldBold>By Molly Aoide<type:text, x:15, y:211, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>Staff Writer<type:text, x:15, y:240, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:378, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>       KNOX EXCLUSION ZONE BORDER,  KY  - At approximately 5 a.m. Wednesday morning, hun- dreds of people infected with the "Knox Virus" broke through military barricades from inside the Exclusion Zone south of Louisville, Ky. Heavy live fire failed to stop the large group's advance.                      Up to 100 Army per- sonnel and civilians were killed, with many hun- dreds wounded. Witnesses report the sounds of battle attracted even more of the infected from a wide area. Both military and refugees near the border pulled back to Louisville.                    Large groups of the infected  attacked  houses in the suburbs throughout the day, moving slowly north towards the city, meeting only sporadic re- sistance, mostly by armed civilians. The streets and bridges out of Louisville quickly filled with panick- ed citizens fleeing over the Ohio River, and traffic jams have  been  reported<type:text, x:180, y:716, r:0, g:0, b:0, a:0.9, scaleX:0.4, scaleY:0.4, autoWidth:375, textTracking:0.5, textLeading:3, font:SdfOldRegular>as far north as Columbus, Ohio, and Indianapolis, Ind. BRANDENBURG DISASTER FUNDS ON THE WAY, SAYS GOVERNOR

[image] - Governor Cal Fairweather speaking in Frankfort yesterday.

FRANKFORT - Governor Cal Fairweather has reassured Brandenburg's mayor that the long-promised federal funds for the rebuilding of Brandenburg are "on the way."
 Despite an overwhelming early response following the tornado on April 18, which saw ample aid provided for residents in the aftermath, promised federal funds for rebuilding have still not arrived, with buildings patched up with wood, and major damage still evident.
 Early warnings meant many residents were taking shelter when the tornado touched down in the northeast part of town, but the high winds killed three residents and injured dozens. The F2 tornado destroyed cars and razed houses. Hundreds of people remain homeless, living in hotels or trailer parks paid for by the state, with others living with relatives or friends. Up to 40%% of residences and 30%% of businesses in the area are uninsured, meaning the cost to the taxpayer could exceed 50 million dollars.

Coalfield, Kentucky\\n\\nA Taste of the:
Coalfield, Kentucky

A Taste of the Wild West

Founded in the 1850s as a stop for travelers heading east, Coalfield became notorious for a series of conflicts between Sheriff Everett Holloway and Irvin Bradshaw and his gang.
The feud culminated with a massive shootout on the night of August 11, 1882, which ended when the Lawman's Distillery caught fire and exploded, taking many buildings with it. No sign of Everett Holloway or Irvin Bradshaw was ever found.

Now you can visit the original site of Coalfield, renovated accurately. Visit our general store, have a drink in the saloons, experience life as a blacksmith, tour period cabins, and see what the Old West was really like!

Come along every Saturday for a reenactment of the shootout between Holloway's lawmen and the Bradshaw gang!

Tour a Future that didn't happen!\\n\\nJ:
Tour a Future that didn't happen!

Just off Adams Road in northern March Ridge sits a fenced area with a small shed and a radio tower.

For decades, this was the entrance to a top secret nuclear bunker, built to house Fort Knox's military leaders.

Built four storeys underground in 1960, with thick steel doors, the bunker was made to withstand a direct nuclear hit on Fort Knox itself.

Space was limited, with beds for only forty people. It's unlikely the bunker would have survived for long without resupply.

Thankfully, armageddon did not arrive.

The bunker was decommissioned in 1991 and is now available for weekend tours!

Book ahead on 943-555-7843.

Note: Tour not suitable for the claustrophobic or young children. Bunker has not been fully checked for asbestos and some forms of poisoning. Waivers must be signed on entry.

<H2> Important <LINE> <TEXT> Mods from B: Important Mods from Build 41 and older builds must be updated for Build 42. You need to enable the "Show unsupported mods" option in Debug mode to run older mods.
<H2> List of mods and filters <LINE> <TE: List of mods and filters On the left is a list of mods. You can filter them to only show enabled mods or your favorites, and search by name, ModID or WorkshopID. To enable a mod, click on its checkbox. To add a mod to your favorites, click on the star.
<H2> Presets and sharing mod lists <LINE: Presets and sharing mod lists To create a mod selection preset, turn on the mods you want to add to the preset, and click SAVE under the list of mods. The DEL button will delete the preset. To share the preset you created, select a preset and click the SHARE button. After that, a line of text with the mods will be added to your clipboard. You can send the text to someone who can add the mods to their game with the ADD button.
<H2> Mod description <LINE> <TEXT> On th: Mod description On the right side of the screen is a description of the selected mod, which includes screenshots of the mod and a description of its parameters. It may also include links to sites that will open in your browser, and links to dependencies for the mod to work, or incompatibilities between this mod and others.
<H2> Mod order <LINE> <TEXT> Using the M: Mod order Using the Mod Order button, you can change the order in which mods are loaded. They can be ordered automatically, or moved using the mouse (by clicking on the move icon and dragging the mod) or a gamepad. Mods towards the top are loaded first. Changing the order of mods may help with errors.
<H2> Map order <LINE> <TEXT> In the case: <H2> Map order <LINE> <TEXT> In the case of map conflicts, the Map Order button will be available. Maps higher on the order will be given priority, and loaded over maps lower down.
